extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, grant applicants, institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page of NIH Extramural Nexus items summarizing recent updates, resources, and reminders about NIH grant policies, application formats, review processes, and data/replication expectations for extramural applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate models (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: “NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose scientifically sound models that best answer the research question; prefer approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential. The phrase emphasizes fit-for-purpose model selection rather than using techniques for novelty alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 application format and expect potential splitting into linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: “Watch NIH’s 6‑minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just‑in‑Time requests.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the specified PF5 application format and be prepared that, after review and prior to Just‑in‑Time, applications may be administratively split into linked awards. Applicants should review the overview to understand formatting and post-review administrative outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format and required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified set of required elements specified by NIH. Treat the format and elements as required components of applications that include a DMS plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research and applications
rubrics_metrics.description: “The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate replication and reproducibility considerations into study design, applications, and award activities. Expect NIH to highlight and potentially prioritize replication/reproducibility efforts and to provide incentives or highlighted topics related to these practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of review outcome category: 'Competitive But Not Discussed'
rubrics_metrics.description: “Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as ‘competitive but not discussed.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that 'competitive but not discussed' indicates the application fell into the middle third of the study section ranking (below a discussion cutoff). Applicants should interpret such scores in context of revised review processes and consider implications for resubmission or clarification in future applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand centralization of NIH peer review (CSR consolidation)
rubrics_metrics.description: “In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) ... we are providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer‑review process.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that NIH peer review processes have been centralized under CSR, with potential effects on review efficiency, competition, and transparency. Applicants and administrators should monitor updates to understand any procedural or timing changes that affect submission and review expectations.
